bib.title: Multimodal Deep Learning, Chapter 2: Introducing the modalities

read.by: manual (source-reader dispatch refused: concurrent subagent limit)

question: What NLP and computer-vision building blocks, datasets, pretraining tasks and benchmarks does multimodal learning rest on?
contributions: Background on word embeddings, seq2seq, attention, the Transformer, BERT/GPT-style pretraining, few-shot learning (NLP); ResNet, EfficientNet, SimCLR, BYOL, ViT (CV); datasets, pretraining tasks and benchmarks (2.3).

results.claim: The book says OpenAI collected more than 250 million text-image pairs to train CLIP and DALL-E.
results.quote: Open AI collected more than 250 million text-images pairs from the internet to train CLIP and DALL-E.
results.note: CONTRADICTED: the CLIP paper (Radford et al. 2021, arXiv 2103.00020) states a dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs.

results.claim: Blindly answering 'yes' to VQA questions gives 87% accuracy, as the book states it.
results.metric: VQA accuracy of always answering yes
results.setup: Section 2.3.3.3 on VQA flaws; attributed to Antol et al. 2015.
results.quote: blindly answering “yes” without reading the rest of the question or looking at the associated image results in a VQA accuracy of 87%
results.note: QUALIFIER DROPPED: Goyal et al. 2017 (arXiv 1612.00837) report 87% only for questions starting with the n-gram 'Do you see a ...', not for the dataset as a whole.

results.claim: SimCLR ResNet-50 (4x) top-1 85.8 and top-5 92.6 in the prose, against 76.5 and 93.2 in the chapter's own table.
results.setup: Section 2.2.6.4, ImageNet comparison of contrastive frameworks.
results.quote: for ResNet-50(4x) top-1 accuracy is 85.8 and top-5 accuracy is 92.6
results.note: Internal inconsistency: Table in the same section gives SimCLR ResNet-50 (4x) 375M params, 76.5 / 93.2. Prose figure not reproduced in notes.

results.claim: Strubell et al. is cited for two different CO2 figures for a big Transformer: 249 t in 2.1 and 284 t (with neural architecture search) in 2.3.3.5.
results.setup: Sections 2.1 and 2.3.3.5, citing Strubell et al. 2019 (a/b).
results.quote: training procedure of a big Transformer with neural architecture search emitted 284t of CO 2
results.note: Different configurations (without and with NAS) may explain the gap; not checked against Strubell et al., so not carried into any note.

results.claim: VQA v2.0 balances VQA by adding complementary images so each question has two images with different answers, about doubling the image-question pairs.
results.quote: has approximately twice the number of image-question pairs
results.note: Agrees with Goyal et al. and with note 07.

results.claim: LAION-400M is curated with CLIP, so it may breed CLIP-like models; Birhane et al. (2021) found explicit and stereotyped pairs in it.
results.note: Reported through the book; Birhane et al. was not read.

results.claim: VALSE tests foil sensitivity across existence, plurality, counting, spatial relations, actions and coreference; foils come from language models, are filtered with NLI and validated by humans, mostly on MS-COCO.
results.quote: task-independent, zero-shot benchmark to assess the extent to which models learn to ground specific linguistic phenomena

results.claim: GQA has 113K images and 22M questions and adds Consistency, Validity and Plausibility measures.
PartiPrompts has over 1,600 English prompts spanning categories and difficulty levels.

limits: Written January 2023: LAION-5B called the biggest open image-text set; model and benchmark lists stop at 2022.
Most of the chapter (word2vec, seq2seq, attention, Transformer, BERT/GPT, ResNet, EfficientNet, SimCLR, BYOL) is general NLP/CV background that belongs to other pillars.
Student seminar text with several errors (CLIP data size, dropped VQA qualifier, SimCLR prose/table mismatch).
practices: Check a dataset for language bias before trusting a VQA score: balance it with complementary pairs (2.3.3.3).
Audit large web-scraped image-text sets for explicit content and stereotypes before training on them (2.3.1).
Use foil-based benchmarks (FOIL-COCO, VALSE) to test whether a model grounds language in the image (2.3.3.4.3-4).

terms.definition: A caption with a single error introduced into a human-annotated one (FOIL-COCO).
Language gives a strong prior that yields good superficial VQA performance without understanding the image.

lineage.work: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (CLIP)
lineage.note: Book gives >250M pairs; the paper says 400M.

lineage.work: Making the V in VQA Matter
lineage.note: Book restates the balanced VQA v2.0 construction and the 87% blind-yes figure, dropping the 'Do you see a' qualifier.
